Implement a Loss-Aversion Point Engine and Reward System using the following architecture:

1. DUAL-CURRENCY SYSTEM:
- XP (Experience Points): Earned ONLY through task completion. Permanent, cumulative, and never lost or docked. Drives overall level and gamer ranks (Unranked -> Iron -> Bronze -> Silver -> Gold -> Platinum -> Diamond -> Ascendant -> Radiant).

opportunities.title: Bug: Trade Republic staking rewards and their tax are not imported
opportunities.description:
## Before you start (required)

### General checklist

- [x] I have removed personal / sensitive data from screenshots and logs
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/issues?q=is:issue) and [discussions](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/discussions) to ensure this is not a duplicate issue

### How are you using Sure?

- [ ] I was a paying Maybe customer (hosted version)
- [ ] I use it on PikaPod, Umbrel or similar (VPS included)
- [x] I am a self-hosted user (local only)

### Self hoster checklist

- Self hosted app commit SHA (find in user menu): bdb280b3b
  - [x] I have confirmed that my app's commit is the latest version of Sure
- Where are you hosting?
  - [ ] Render
  - [ ] Docker Compose
  - [ ] Umbrel
  - [ ] PikaPod
  - [x] Other (please specify): TrueNAS SCALE app (Docker)

---

## Bug description

Trade Republic pays crypto staking rewards (Solana in my case) every week, and charges the tax on each reward to the cash account. The account statement lists every tax debit, for example:

```
Imposte · Staking Reward XF000SOL0012 Solana, quantity: 0.024461
```

Neither the reward nor the tax is on the Trade Republic timeline, so the sync cannot import them:

- **Crypto account:** the holding is correct, because it comes from the positions snapshot. The trades, though, add up to less than the position, since the reward coins have no trade. Cost basis and the holding's history miss them.
- **Cash account:** the current balance is correct, because it is anchored to Trade Republic's cash. The balance history, though, misses the small weekly tax debits, and drifts further from the statement each week before today.

On my account the statement has 46 weekly tax debits between November 2025 and October 2026. I read both timeline topics in full (`timelineTransactions` and `timelineActivityLog`, 61 pages). They contain no event for any reward or tax debit. Everything else on the statement reconciles line by line with what Sure imports from the timeline.

### To Reproduce

1. Hold a crypto asset with staking enabled at Trade Republic (for example Solana) for a few weeks.
2. Sync the Trade Republic connection.
3. Compare the crypto trades with the position quantity, and the cash account's history with the monthly statement.
4. See that the reward coins and the weekly "Staking Reward" tax debits are missing.

### Expected behavior

Staking rewards import as crypto buys at no cost, and their tax as a cash debit. If Trade Republic does not expose them outside the statement, the limitation should at least be documented, so users know why the crypto trades and the cash history differ from the statement.

opportunities.title: feat: implement BucketPerps V1 synthetic perpetual protocol
opportunities.description:
## Summary

Implement **BucketPerps V1**, a standalone synthetic leveraged trading protocol inspired by the early-1900s bucket-shop model and the core economic primitive demonstrated by Papertrade.

**Papertrade/Martingaler mechanics are the baseline for the house, margin, settlement, and FIFO model unless this issue explicitly defines a BucketPerps deviation.** Implementation choices that are not explicit deviations should not silently change those baseline mechanics.

BucketPerps does not use an orderbook or AMM for execution.

The protocol itself takes the opposite side of every trader position.

```text
Trader LONG  <-> BucketPerps SHORT
Trader SHORT <-> BucketPerps LONG
```

Positions execute against an authenticated external reference price rather than against available market liquidity.

BucketPerps therefore provides:

```text
synthetic leveraged exposure
no orderbook
no execution AMM
no external LP requirement
no funding-rate price adjustment
no synthetic execution spread
```

The system may bootstrap with:

```text
house reserve = 0
external LP capital = 0
```

Cash-funded trader margin is real capital. Existing unpaid FIFO claims may also be committed as claim-funded trading margin; claim funding does not create cash or increase the house reserve.

Synthetic notional and unrealized trader profit do not need to be fully collateralized.

Only **realized unpaid trader profit** originates FIFO debt. Reusing an existing claim as margin preserves that debt origin; surviving claim-funded value follows the payout/requeue rules below.

When the house cannot immediately pay all realized profit, unpaid profit enters a strict FIFO liability queue and is serviced from future house gains.

---

# Architecture

BucketPerps is a standalone protocol and is not part of the Statics Diamond.

**BucketPerps V1 SHALL use EIP-2535 Diamond architecture.** This is a ratified protocol architecture decision.

```text
                  Statics PositionNFT
                         |
                  ownership authority
                         |
                         v
                  BucketPerps Core
                         |
        +----------------+----------------+
        |                |                |
     Trading          Settlement        Staking
        |                |                |
        v                v                v
  open positions    house reserve      wSTATICS
                    + FIFO queue
        |
        v
 StaticsExecutionOracle
        |
        v
 Chainlink Data Streams
```

BucketPerps owns all:

- trading state;
- market configuration;
- margin accounting;
- open interest;
- positions;
- leverage;
- liquidations;
- realized PnL;
- house reserve;
- FIFO profit liabilities;
- BucketPerps reward-token staking accounting;
- loss rewards;
- protocol revenue;
- buyback accounting.

Statics and `statics-oracle` MUST NOT contain BucketPerps economic accounting.

---

# External dependencies

## 1. `EqualFiLabs/statics-oracle#17`

BucketPerps execution depends on the dedicated Data Streams execution oracle.

BucketPerps MUST NOT independently implement:

- Chainlink report decoding;
- Chainlink signature verification;
- feed selection;
- deterministic report-window selection;
- report-shopping defenses;
- sequencer-health evaluation;
- price normalization.

Instead:

```text
BucketPerps
    |
    | marketId + report bundle
    v
StaticsExecutionOracle
    |
    v
ExecutionPrice
```

The execution oracle returns the deterministic authenticated price used for the transaction.

The same execution primitive MUST be used for:

```text
long open
long close
short open
short close
liquidation
```

There MUST NOT be a fallback to:

```text
DEX spot
Basket NAV
Chainlink Data Feed
cached price
admin price
single-exchange BBO
```

during normal settlement.

## Permissionless submission and licensed report delivery

Users and alternative frontends MUST be able to submit opens, closes, and permissionless liquidations directly to BucketPerps. No mandatory central relayer, private submission gateway, relayer signature, or relayer-controlled size-priority policy may authorize trades. Ordinary chain ordering and gas competition still apply.

Our licensed Chainlink subscription, credentials, and report-delivery service are not a public data-access entitlement. This issue does not require public subscription access or unrestricted redistribution.

Independently obtained signed reports MUST be accepted through the same onchain validation path when they match the market's approved stream ID, schema, deterministic signed-window selection, verifier, expiry, and sequencer requirements. Reports need not originate from our endpoint or carry our service's signature. A Chainlink signature alone does not authorize an arbitrary stream.

---

## 2. Statics PositionNFT

BucketPerps MUST NOT issue a separate account NFT.

The canonical **Statics PositionNFT** is the ownership root for BucketPerps accounts.

BucketPerps state is keyed by Statics PositionNFT `tokenId`.

Conceptually:

```solidity
mapping(uint256 positionId => BucketPerpsAccount) accounts;
```

NOT:

```solidity
mapping(address trader => BucketPerpsAccount) accounts;
```

Authorization MUST derive dynamically from the Statics PositionNFT.

The current `ownerOf(positionId)` is the ownership root for the BucketPerps financial account.

ERC-721 transfer approvals such as `getApproved(positionId)` and `isApprovedForAll(owner, caller)` MUST NOT automatically become authority to trade, withdraw margin, claim FIFO, stake/unstake, or otherwise control BucketPerps financial state.

If delegated financial control is added, it must use an explicit BucketPerps-specific authorization mechanism.

BucketPerps MUST NOT persist an authoritative account-owner address that requires synchronization when the NFT transfers.

---

---

# PositionNFT transfer semantics

A BucketPerps account is part of the financial account represented by the Statics PositionNFT.

Example:

```text
Statics PositionNFT #1234
    |
    +-- BucketPerps margin
    +-- BTC long
    +-- ETH short
```

# Core trading primitive

BucketPerps executes synthetic leveraged positions directly against the house.

There is no matching engine.

There is no maker order.

There is no requirement for another trader to take the opposite side.

Example:

```text

$1,000 margin
10x leverage
$10,000 BTC long

BucketPerps records:

Trader synthetic BTC exposure: +$10,000
House synthetic BTC exposure:  -$10,000
```

No BTC is purchased.

No `$10,000` counterparty collateral must be reserved.

The position's PnL is calculated from:

```text
entry execution price
exit execution price
notional
direction
```

# Margin funding

Queued FIFO claims MUST be usable as trading margin in addition to cash margin.

- Track cash and claim margin distinctly; committing a claim is not a cash deposit.
- A committed claim amount cannot remain simultaneously withdrawable, payable from FIFO, or reusable in another position.
- Claim-funded losses cancel debt and do not add cash to the house.
- Surviving claim-funded value and net winnings follow baseline payout/requeue rules, including losing consumed FIFO priority and rejoining the tail when still unpaid.
- Cash-funded principal returns from cash margin; committed original claim value is not guaranteed immediate cash redemption.
- All claims and funded positions remain associated with their Statics PositionNFT account.

Whether one position can mix cash and claim margin remains to be specified.

# Liquidation

Liquidation MUST be permissionless and use the same authenticated `StaticsExecutionOracle` path as opens and closes. The liquidator cannot select the execution price.

Mirror Papertrade's buffered hard-bust model:

- Liquidation occurs before zero equity using a configured price buffer. Approximately 5 basis points of asset-price movement is the reference baseline for testing.
- At or beyond bust, the entire isolated margin is forfeited, including remaining equity.
- An owner close executed at or beyond bust MUST use the same liquidation accounting.
- Cash margin, FIFO empty: carve an initial 2.00% fee from forfeited margin; the remainder becomes house capital.
- Cash margin, FIFO active: waive the fee; retain the full forfeited cash margin for FIFO servicing.
- Claim margin: cancel the full committed claim; no liquidation fee or cash inflow is created.

We may operate a keeper, but liquidation MUST work without it or our frontend/report endpoint. Keeper compensation remains unresolved. Test protocol-funded operations versus a bounded incentive carved from an eligible existing fee; do not silently add a bounty or divert cash owed to other accounts or FIFO claimants.

The hard-bust model is agreed. Final buffers, leverage limits, and keeper compensation require execution and economic testing. Copying a nominal 5 bps from Hyperliquid BBO execution does not qualify Chainlink execution.

# Losing settlement

Ordinary losing closes use raw adverse PnL without an additional trader surcharge. Return/credit unused cash margin to the PositionNFT account.

Mirror the baseline fee and queue ordering:

- Cash loss, FIFO empty: carve 2.00% from the realized house gain; retain the remainder.
- Cash loss, FIFO active: waive the fee; retain the full loss for FIFO servicing.
- Claim loss: cancel lost claim value instead of recording cash gain. A loss fee is payable only from genuinely available cash when FIFO is empty and cash covers surviving claim payout plus fee; otherwise waive it.
- A close at/past bust follows full-margin liquidation accounting.

Future loss-derived cash gains MUST service FIFO before discretionary reserve overflow. Debt cancellation MUST NOT be represented as new cash.

---

# Winning settlement

Return/credit cash-funded principal immediately; cash principal MUST NOT enter FIFO.

Apply the profit haircut, then the 1.90% win fee, then pay net profit from available house cash without bypassing older FIFO claims. Unpaid net realized profit becomes FIFO debt.

Claim-funded positions retain baseline payout/requeue rules. Their original committed claim is not newly deposited cash or guaranteed immediate cash principal.

Fee recipients receive cash only when baseline reserve/FIFO rules permit. An unfunded win fee does not create a separate deferred fee IOU. FIFO harvest MUST NOT charge the win fee twice.

# Strict FIFO profit queue

FIFO ordering is a core protocol invariant.

Use monotonically increasing claim IDs.

Conceptually:

```solidity
struct ProfitClaim {
    uint256 positionId;
    uint256 remaining;
}
```

Do NOT use an authoritative claimant wallet address.

The claim belongs to the Statics PositionNFT.

Therefore if the NFT is transferred while the claim is waiting:

```text
Alice owns NFT -> claim enters FIFO
Alice sells NFT to Bob
FIFO later pays claim
Bob owns economic right to payment
```

Required queue behavior:

- monotonically increasing claim ID;
- deterministic queue head;
- strict FIFO ordering;
- partial head fulfillment allowed;
- partial fulfillment does not lose queue priority;
- later claims cannot skip the head;
- no privileged reordering;
- no double payment;
- claim remains associated with PositionNFT;
- outstanding FIFO liability is publicly observable;
- trading may continue while FIFO debt exists.

A permissionless processing function MAY bound the number of queue entries processed per transaction.

It MUST NOT allow the processor to choose which claims are serviced.

# House reserve

BucketPerps uses the Papertrade/Martingaler house-reserve model.

The house reserve MAY start at zero.

The reserve does not need to collateralize:

```text
total open interest
unrealized trader profit
worst-case theoretical synthetic liability
```

The reserve pays realized net winning profit synchronously where possible. Unpaid net profit enters FIFO; surviving claim-funded value follows the claim-margin rules rather than an immediate cash-principal guarantee.

Track at least the house reserve and outstanding FIFO liability. Exact internal accounting should preserve the baseline Papertrade/Martingaler settlement model rather than introduce a new margin model.

## House surplus threshold

BucketPerps has an admin-configurable house surplus threshold.

Initial deployment target:

```text
approximately $1,000,000
```

The threshold may be raised as actual usage, open interest, payout behavior, and FIFO experience justify retaining a larger bankroll.

Rules:

```text
FIFO > 0
-> no house-surplus distribution

FIFO == 0 and houseReserve <= houseSurplusThreshold
-> house gains remain in the reserve

FIFO == 0 and houseReserve > houseSurplusThreshold
-> excess may be distributed according to configured surplus allocation
```

This threshold is intentionally a simple governed parameter, not an automated solvency formula.

The exact surplus-distribution split is configurable and is not fixed by this issue.

# Reserve waterfall

When the house receives realized gains, the baseline settlement model applies.

BucketPerps adds only the following surplus rule:

```text
FIFO debt exists?
    |
   yes
    |
    v
no discretionary house-surplus distribution

FIFO cleared
    |
    v
retain house bankroll through houseSurplusThreshold
    |
    v
excess may be distributed under configured surplus settings
```

Apply the explicit fee bases and ordering below. The approximately $1M threshold controls discretionary surplus distribution, not payment of otherwise eligible trading fees. FIFO and cash-availability restrictions still apply.

# Profit haircut and BucketPerps fees

Mirror Papertrade's documented October 21, 2026 contract-set-2 haircut: favorable-move deadband, small-move holdback, then asymmetric gain scaling. The reference deadband is 0.2 bps. Scaling uses configured reference notional rather than actual trade size, so splitting a trade cannot avoid its percentage haircut. Preserve monotonic payouts and standard/off-hours preset-curve behavior.

Qualify market parameters against Chainlink report timing and execution. Final curve coefficients and preset-switch operation remain launch decisions.

## Winning profit fee

Initial fee: **1.90% of profit after the haircut**, not notional, margin, or pre-haircut profit.

```text
1.00% -> BucketPerps reward-token stakers
0.70% -> BucketPerps protocol
0.20% -> Statics Operators
----------------------------
1.90% total
```

Each percentage applies to adjusted profit. These are initial configurable parameters. Net winning profit is 98.10% of adjusted profit.

## Loss and liquidation fees

Initial loss/liquidation fee remains **2.00%**, with the cash/claim and FIFO waiver conditions above. The 1.90% reduction applies only to wins.

Specify the separate loss/liquidation recipient allocation before implementation; the 1.00% / 0.70% / 0.20% win-fee split does not by itself allocate a 2.00% fee. Any keeper carve-out must be specified together with that allocation.

Fees MUST NOT charge cash principal, manufacture cash from cancelled claims, skip FIFO, or charge another win fee on harvest.

## Reference mechanics

Use the discussed documented mechanics as a fixed reference rather than silently following future Papertrade changes:

- [Asymmetric impact](https://docs.papertrade.xyz/how/asymmetric-impact/)
- [Wins and losses](https://docs.papertrade.xyz/learn/wins-losses/)
- [Liquidations](https://docs.papertrade.xyz/learn/liquidations/)
- [Protocol changes](https://docs.papertrade.xyz/dev/protocol-changes/)

Specify and test curve parameters, fee rounding, settings changes affecting open positions, and liquidation timing before production launch.

```text
1.00x base multiplier
```

# Critical invariants

Implementation and tests MUST preserve at least:

### Baseline settlement invariant

BucketPerps preserves the Papertrade/Martingaler house, margin, realized-PnL, and FIFO model except where this issue explicitly defines a deviation.

### FIFO invariant

Only unpaid realized trader profit originates FIFO debt. Claim-margin reuse cannot create cash, duplicate debt, or preserve consumed FIFO priority. Cash principal never enters FIFO. FIFO ordering cannot be bypassed.

### Ownership invariant

BucketPerps account ownership follows the current Statics PositionNFT owner without wallet-state migration.

### Transfer invariant

A PositionNFT transfer does not require BucketPerps financial-state migration.

### Closure invariant

A PositionNFT cannot be closed or burned while unresolved BucketPerps state remains.

### Oracle invariant

Every price-sensitive execution uses the exact authenticated price returned by `StaticsExecutionOracle`.

### Reward-token backing invariant

```text
BucketPerps reward-token supply
==
STATICS backing
```

### Public-wrap-cap invariant

Permissionless public wrapping cannot exceed the configured public wrapping cap.

### Flat loss-reward invariant

Loss-reward issuance uses the configured flat `lossRewardRate` and does not change automatically with reserve size, FIFO depth, solvency state, or house surplus threshold.

### Operator-weight invariant

BucketPerps staking revenue uses effective Operator-weighted stake while raw reward-token stake remains unchanged.

### Prospective multiplier invariant

Operator multiplier transitions cannot retroactively change already-accrued BucketPerps staking rewards.

- [ ] Add restricted 1:1 STATICS-backed BucketPerps reward token (working-name implementation may use `wSTATICS`).
- [ ] Add public wrapping cap initialized to zero.
- [ ] Add fully backed protocol/loss-reward issuance path beyond the public wrap cap if required.
- [ ] Add PositionNFT-keyed BucketPerps reward-token staking.
- [ ] Integrate Statics Operator activation weighting into BucketPerps staking.
- [ ] Add flat configurable lossRewardRate with fully backed issuance.
- [ ] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Add fuzz/property tests.
- [ ] Add protocol invariant suite.

- [ ] Add irreversible finalizeProtocol with retained knobs/fixed migration.
- [ ] Add USDG settlement and fixed future USDstx conversion capability.
- [ ] Add selector-map/upgrade/storage-preservation/finalization tests.
- [ ] Add Robinhood fork tests.
- [ ] Add deployment scripts.
- [ ] Add deployment manifest/evidence.
- [ ] Add protocol documentation and threat model.
- [ ] Complete adversarial security review before production deployment.

---

## Acceptance criteria

BucketPerps V1 is complete when:

1. A Statics PositionNFT owner can control the associated BucketPerps financial account, and ordinary ERC-721 marketplace approvals do not automatically grant BucketPerps financial authority.

2. BucketPerps takes the synthetic opposite side without requiring an orderbook, execution AMM, or externally funded LP.

3. The house, margin, realized-PnL, and FIFO mechanics preserve the Papertrade/Martingaler baseline except for deviations explicitly specified in this issue.

4. FIFO debt originates only unpaid realized trader profit; claim-margin payout/requeue preserves that origin and cannot turn cancelled claims into cash or queue cash principal.

5. Future house gains service FIFO according to the baseline FIFO model.

6. Trading can continue while FIFO debt exists unless separately disabled by market/risk controls.

7. BucketPerps accounts are keyed to Statics PositionNFT IDs rather than wallet addresses.

8. Transfer of a PositionNFT transfers economic control of the complete associated BucketPerps account without financial-state migration, subject to existing Statics transfer-lock rules.

9. Active BucketPerps state prevents the PositionNFT from being closed/burned.

10. Price-sensitive opens, closes, and liquidations use the authenticated execution-price primitive provided by `StaticsExecutionOracle`.

11. The BucketPerps reward token is fully backed 1:1 by STATICS at all times.

12. Permissionless public wrapping respects its configurable cap, initialized to zero; zero cap preserves backed reward issuance and unwraps.

13. Loss rewards use a flat configurable `lossRewardRate` and do not vary automatically with house reserve size, FIFO depth, solvency state, or house surplus threshold.

14. BucketPerps reward-token staking and accrued BucketPerps staking revenue belong to the PositionNFT account.

15. BucketPerps staking applies the existing Statics Operator activation multiplier to effective staking weight without changing raw stake.

16. Operator multiplier changes settle accrued rewards before changing effective weight so historical BucketPerps revenue is never retroactively reweighted.

17. Existing Statics Genesis/Operator link and transfer-lock behavior remains unchanged by BucketPerps.

18. The initial house surplus threshold is configurable, targets approximately $1M at launch, blocks discretionary surplus distribution while FIFO exists, and may be raised as actual usage warrants.

19. The configurable initial win fee is 1.90% of adjusted profit: 1.00% stakers / 0.70% protocol / 0.20% Operators. The separate loss/liquidation fee remains 2.00% with the specified cash/claim and FIFO waiver rules. Haircut precedes win fee; fee routing cannot manufacture cash, charge principal, or bypass FIFO.

20. The Operator share routes to `EqualFiLabs/operator-fee-router` without BucketPerps duplicating Operator-NFT reward accounting.

21. Unit, fuzz/property, invariant, and Robinhood Chain integration suites pass.

22. The architecture remains standalone from Statics core economic accounting while using Statics PositionNFT as the transferable ownership root.

23. BucketPerps V1 is an EIP-2535 Diamond with canonical entry point, namespaced storage, verified selector routing, controlled upgrades, and irreversible finalizeProtocol preserving only specified knobs and fixed migration.

24. Queued claims can fund margin without duplicate debt, duplicate use, cash fabrication, or retention of consumed queue priority.

25. Users can submit directly, without a mandatory relayer or our report endpoint; independently obtained approved-stream reports follow identical verification rules.

26. USDG is the launch settlement asset; fixed atomic USDstx migration preserves normalized value and FIFO order and is independent of Phase 3 launch timing.

27. Guardian emergency controls and the explicit safety-focused authority/timelock matrix are implemented and tested.

---

## Decisions still required before implementation or launch

- Exact launch leverage, OI, minimum/maximum sizes, haircut coefficients/preset switching, and liquidation buffer, qualified against Chainlink execution timing.
- Keeper compensation and the recipient allocation of the separate 2.00% loss/liquidation fee.

- Public-wrap capacity accounting if public wrapping is ever enabled.

The agreed economic baseline is the haircut and buffered full-margin liquidation model described above; these open decisions do not authorize silently changing that model.

opportunities.title: Prevent hosting cash rewards from replaying on reload or retry
opportunities.description:
## Summary

More Hosting Deals can pay cash from retryable Enabled handling. Its already-paid flag resets on load, and completion is marked only after the payment loop.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable More Hosting Deals with active ServerDeal items and receive the noon payout.
2. Save and reload during noon with the setting enabled.
3. Trace cold-start Enabled handling reaching payout again.
4. Exercise a failure after one credit but before the payment loop finishes.

Replay paths are verified in source. A Unity cash-balance reproduction has not been performed.

## Expected Behavior

A defined scheduled reward is not paid again merely because a save reloads or a catch-up handler is retried.

## Actual Behavior

The resettable Boolean permits a noon reload payout. A partially successful loop can repeat earlier transactions on another attempt.

## Environment

- Trainer: 5.6.0, develop 8064eb8f22ece9451561c4bff3aa10e534944691.
- Game target: current vendored Software Inc. Beta 1.8.42 assemblies.
- Deployment: Workshop source compilation and the DLL build.
- Review: source and decompiled native assembly; full Unity reproduction is identified separately below.

## Additional Context

Priority recommendation: P2.

Evidence: [payment](https://github.com/Trawis/T5B1/blob/8064eb8f22ece9451561c4bff3aa10e534944691/Trainer_v5/Trainer.Source/Features/MarketFeatures.cs#L35), [timing](https://github.com/Trawis/T5B1/blob/8064eb8f22ece9451561c4bff3aa10e534944691/Trainer_v5/Trainer.Source/Features/MarketFeatures.cs#L117), ResetGameState and Enabled/Hour registry entries. This contradicts the documented repeatability requirement of Enabled actions.

Suggested approach: separate deal catch-up from payout. The smallest option pays cash only through the scheduled hourly path; explicitly decide whether immediate noon-on-enable payment must remain. If preserving that catch-up, define saved cycle/payment identity, eligibility changes, migration for old saves and partial-failure semantics before coding. Do not assume one saved Boolean establishes exactly-once payment.

Acceptance conditions:
- Cover save before/after payout, noon reload, repeated reload, enable/disable at noon and the next normal noon.
- A partial attempt cannot repeat already-applied credits through retry.
- Preserve reward amounts and eligible deal types.
- Keep financial side effects out of retryable catch-up unless made demonstrably safe.
- Do not add a general transaction framework.
- Report focused tests and actual in-game validation separately.

Related: #266, #336, PR #418, #344. #246 concerned completed deal-type detection and is not this bug.

## Bug description

Trade Republic pays crypto staking rewards (Solana in my case) every week, and charges the tax on each reward to the cash account. The account statement lists every tax debit, for example:

```
Imposte · Staking Reward XF000SOL0012 Solana, quantity: 0.024461
```

Neither the reward nor the tax is on the Trade Republic timeline, so the sync cannot import them:

- **Crypto account:** the holding is correct, because it comes from the positions snapshot. The trades, though, add up to less than the position, since the reward coins have no trade. Cost basis and the holding's history miss them.
- **Cash account:** the current balance is correct, because it is anchored to Trade Republic's cash. The balance history, though, misses the small weekly tax debits, and drifts further from the statement each week before today.

On my account the statement has 46 weekly tax debits between November 2025 and October 2026. I read both timeline topics in full (`timelineTransactions` and `timelineActivityLog`, 61 pages). They contain no event for any reward or tax debit. Everything else on the statement reconciles line by line with what Sure imports from the timeline.

### To Reproduce

1. Hold a crypto asset with staking enabled at Trade Republic (for example Solana) for a few weeks.
2. Sync the Trade Republic connection.
3. Compare the crypto trades with the position quantity, and the cash account's history with the monthly statement.
4. See that the reward coins and the weekly "Staking Reward" tax debits are missing.

### Expected behavior

Staking rewards import as crypto buys at no cost, and their tax as a cash debit. If Trade Republic does not expose them outside the statement, the limitation should at least be documented, so users know why the crypto trades and the cash history differ from the statement.

opportunities.description:
### Issue filing prerequisites

- [x] I've checked the [documentation](https://docs.invoiceshelf.com/).
- [x] I've looked for similar issues both Open and Closed.
- [x] I've tried clearing both cache and cookies in my browser or tried opening the app in the Incognito/InPrivate window.

### Describe the bug

Recording a payment that fully covers a draft invoice changes its status from DRAFT to COMPLETED, although the invoice has never been sent. It is no longer identifiable as a draft, and the completed status suggests that the invoice is finalized and, depending on the editing settings, no longer editable. There is no longer a draft status to indicate that work such as sending the invoice is still pending.

Reducing or deleting that payment can then change the same invoice back to DRAFT and make it editable again, depending on the configured editing restrictions. A payment correction can therefore reopen an invoice that appeared to be finalized, without any explicit action to reopen it.

### Steps to Reproduce the issue

1. Set retrospective edits to be disabled after sending an invoice.
2. Create a draft invoice with a positive total and leave it unsent.
3. Record a payment covering the full invoice amount.
4. Open the invoice and check its status and edit permission.
5. Reduce or delete the payment, then check the invoice status and edit permission again.

### Expected behaviour

The invoice remains DRAFT, its paid_status becomes PAID, and the recorded payment remains associated with it. Its draft status continues to indicate that it has not yet been sent. Later payment corrections update the payment status without implicitly finalizing or reopening the draft.

Editing follows the configured retrospective edit setting: a restriction based on sending should not lock an unsent draft, while payment-based restrictions should still apply.

### Actual behaviour

The invoice becomes COMPLETED solely because it was fully paid. With editing disabled after sending, it can no longer be edited despite never having been sent. Its status hides the fact that it is still an unsent draft and gives the impression that no further action is needed.

Reducing or deleting the payment changes it back to DRAFT; with the same setting, it becomes editable again.

Part of the relay peering work in #931.

## Scope

The source (selling) side of paid peering, using nostream's existing payments processors — the same machinery as admission fees:

- Settlement is detected via the existing processor callbacks; on settlement the peer's feed access activates until the end of the paid period.
- Before expiry, the source offers a renewal invoice.
- If the period lapses unpaid, the feed is suspended — stored data and sync state are kept, so resuming is a payment, not a re-sync from zero.

## Acceptance

- A paid peering relationship completes end-to-end: authenticate → invoice → settlement → feed active for exactly the paid period.
- An unpaid lapse suspends the feed; paying the renewal resumes it without re-reconciliation.
- Invoice/settlement state per peer is recorded for the admin console.
